newsitem.title: USA: Fund managers bolster U.S. debt durations - survey.
newsitem.headline: Fund managers bolster U.S. debt durations - survey.

text.p: Money managers again extended durations in U.S. portfolio structures over the past week but maintained relatively short duration exposure overall, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"Money managers have moved closer to neutral after being about as short as they get as recently as two weeks again," the report said.
In the week ended May 13, the cash/assets ratio fell to 8.87 percent from 9.02 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 6.62 percent from 6.50 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index rose to 98.69 percent from 97.73 percent on an arithmetic basis and fell to 98.05 percent from 98.10 percent on a weighted basis.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index advanced to 4.96 from 4.84 on an arithmetic basis. It slipped to 4.57 from 4.80 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
Four percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 12 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active decreased to 4.00 from 4.67.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
